items.headline: At what point do we decide AI’s risks outweigh its promise?
items.dek: In June 2015, Sam Altman told a tech conference, “I think that AI will probably, most likely, sort of lead to the end of the world. But in the meantime, there will be great companies created with serious machine learning.”
items.outlet: Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research (SIEPR)
items.author: Dave Gilson
items.caption: SIEPR article opening: the fuller spoken version of the quote, followed by 'did not appear to be joking. In the next breath, he announced that he’d just funded a new venture focused on “AI safety research.” That company was OpenAI' (1320x970).
items.notes: Matches the video auto-captions almost word-for-word (captions have 'probably like most likely' where SIEPR has 'probably, most likely,'). 'That company was OpenAI' is SIEPR's interpretation, not Altman's words in the talk. Article 'originally published May 29, 2024 by Stanford GSB Insights'. Ties the quote to economist Charles (Chad) Jones's paper 'The AI Dilemma: Growth versus Existential Risk' (AER: Insights 2024, 6(4): 575-590, doi 10.1257/aeri.20230570) -- great bridge for the economy module.

facts.claim: Exact contemporaneous wording (Business Insider): "AI will probably most likely lead to the end of the world, but in the meantime, there'll be great companies."
facts.source: Business Insider, Matt Weinberger, published 2015-06-05 00:09 UTC (June 4, 2015 US time)

facts.claim: Said by Sam Altman, then president of Y Combinator, on Thursday June 4, 2015, during an onstage fireside chat with Airbnb's Mike Curtis (VP of engineering / CTO) at Airbnb's Open Air 2015 conference -- about six months before OpenAI was announced (December 2015).
facts.source: Business Insider ('speaking Thursday at Airbnb's Open Air 2015 conference'); TechRadar 2026; New Yorker 2026 ('In December, 2015, hours before OpenAI was publicly announced')

facts.claim: Fuller spoken version: “I think that AI will probably, most likely, sort of lead to the end of the world. But in the meantime, there will be great companies created with serious machine learning.”
facts.source: Stanford SIEPR (Dave Gilson, 2024-05-31); matches YouTube auto-captions of the talk at ~8:46

facts.claim: In the next breath he said he had 'actually just agreed to fund a company that is not even really a company sort of a semi company semi- nonprofit uh doing AI Safety Research' (auto-captions); BI: 'Altman shared that he recently invested in a company doing "AI safety research"'. SIEPR: 'That company was OpenAI'.
facts.source: YouTube auto-captions ~9:00 of d6lDZpvHAoo; Business Insider; SIEPR

facts.claim: Same talk: "If I were Barack Obama, I would commit maybe $100 billion to R&D of AI safety initiatives."

Same talk (auto-captions, ~38:20): on brain-scale compute, 'maybe it takes us till 2030 to get there um it's not it's not 100 years away and we'll figure out the algorithm' ... 'right now the answer is we have no idea' how to make AI safe.
facts.source: YouTube auto-generated captions (machine transcription) of the Open Air 2015 fireside chat re-upload

facts.claim: Feb 25, 2015, Altman's blog: "Development of superhuman machine intelligence (SMI) [1] is probably the greatest threat to the continued existence of humanity."
Economist Chad Jones: with log utility, people 'are willing to take a one-in-three chance of killing everyone to get a 50-fold increase in consumption'.
facts.source: Stanford SIEPR summary of Jones, 'The AI Dilemma: Growth versus Existential Risk', AER: Insights 2024, 6(4): 575-590

facts.claim: Jones: if AI spurs 10% annual growth, global incomes rise more than 50-fold over 40 years (vs. US real per-capita GDP doubling in the past 40 years).
Jones: 'cutting mortality in half suddenly turns your willingness to accept existential risk from 4 percent to 25 percent or even more.'
The quote went viral again in 2026: Tom's Guide (Jan 8, 2026) and TechRadar Pro 'Quote of the day' (June 15, 2026) both ran it in headlines.

(Tangential) New Yorker, 2016: Altman said 'I have guns, gold, potassium iodide, antibiotics, batteries, water, gas masks from the Israeli Defense Force, and a big patch of land in Big Sur I can fly to' -- citing scenarios incl. 'A.I. that attacks us'.
facts.source: Tad Friend, 'Sam Altman’s Manifest Destiny', The New Yorker (2016-10-03 online)
